question.value: Can a branched alkyl molecule (iso-propyl cyanide) be detected in the ISM, and how does its abundance compare with its straight-chain isomer and with chemical model predictions?

evidence.quote: We report an interstellar detection of a branched alkyl molecule, iso-propyl cyanide (i-C$_3$H$_7$CN), with an abundance 0.4 times that of its straight-chain structural isomer.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00017.S.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 84.1-110.7 GHz in four overlapping setups; four 1875 MHz spectral windows each; 244 kHz channels smoothed to 488 kHz

evidence.quote: The full frequency range between 84.1 and 110.7 GHz was covered with four slightly overlapping spectral setups.
The channel spacing was 244 kHz, but the spectra were smoothed to 488 kHz (1.7–1.3 km s$^{-1}$).
About 50 and 120 transitions of *i*-PrCN and *n*-PrCN, respectively, are detected toward the northern hot core

findings_qualitative.value: Branched i-PrCN detected with abundance comparable to its straight-chain isomer, suggesting branched molecules may be generally abundant in star-forming regions

evidence.quote: This detection suggests that branched carbon-chain molecules may be generally abundant in the ISM.

findings_qualitative.value: Model forms both isomers on grain ices via radical addition with different dominant pathways

evidence.quote: both isomers are produced within or upon dust grain ice mantles through the addition of molecular radicals, albeit via differing reaction pathways
